name: ref_1
description: First physical print of peg-targets-3x3-12.5mm, four 3x3 ChArUco boards to cut out and place on the ACME disc. Labelled 'ref 1' on the sheet itself.

printer.scaling: INFERRED 'fit to printable area' or equivalent -- see _provenance.scale

mounting: repositionable (sticky-note) adhesive, so pieces can be moved between placements

_provenance.measured: Derived from readings_mm against the OUTER nominals. If the inference in what_was_measured is wrong, every number in measured is wrong with it.
_provenance.square_mm: Derive from the measured spans, not from a ruler on one square. charuco_0001's entry in ../README.md shows the calibration data measuring the board better than the calipers did.
_provenance.anisotropy: +0.273 % +- 0.079, x wider than y, 3.4 sigma -- but n=3, so the sd is itself soft, and six readings were asked for. charuco_0001 came out +0.15 %. Outer-edge readings are inflated by ink spread at both ends, but by the same absolute amount on two equal baselines, so the RATIO is unbiased even though the absolute scale is not.
_provenance.printer: Record the make and the driver's scaling setting. 'Fit to page' is the usual way a print silently changes scale between runs.
_provenance.what_was_measured: INFERENCE, not a statement by the operator, and everything below depends on it. Four candidate nominals were tested for self-consistency: the measured diagonal must equal sqrt((sx^2+sy^2)/2) times its own nominal. Outer printed edges predict the diagonal to 0.074 %; the interior chessboard corners the sheet advertises miss by 1.284 %, seventeen times worse. A second candidate, matching interior corners, fits to 0.113 % but implies a 45.6 % OVERSIZE print of a letter sheet onto letter paper, which is impossible. The small reading scatter (sd 0.055-0.130 mm on the axes) also says a real edge was seated on rather than a virtual corner, which scatters 0.33 mm. Confirm before relying on it.
_provenance.scale: 4.97 % UNDERSIZE, uniform 0.95028. Almost certainly 'fit to printable area': a uniform 0.9503 on a 215.9 x 279.4 mm page leaves 5.37 mm side and 6.95 mm top/bottom margins, which is an ordinary printer's unprintable border. The sheet's content is inset 15 mm, so a 100 % reprint clips nothing.
_provenance.shear_deg: None detected. The diagonals differ by -0.177 mm against a 2-sigma floor of 0.840 mm, which would be -0.070 deg and 43 um across one cut piece.

readings_mm._what_was_seated_on: the printed boards' OUTER edges, not the interior chessboard corners the sheet's own nominals describe. Inferred, not stated -- see _provenance.what_was_measured.
